title: Choose the concept for the new RepoDigger view
question: Your palettes are fixed in every option: Black/Blue/Cyan, Blue/White/Pink, and more, switchable live. This picks the idea underneath them. The roll assigned Core Log; keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Core Log
options.thesis: Each answer is drilled through the code and shown as a core: symbols stacked by depth, beside the graph they came from. Ships with your Black/Blue/Cyan and Blue/White/Pink themes plus more, switchable live.
options.viewport: Three standard panels: graph, the answer's core log, and chat. The lit path is drawn as a vertical drill line.
options.risk: Adds a third column, so the graph gets narrower. The core metaphor leans on the product's name.

raised.raise: Rank comes from one system only: depth in the log, never mixed shadows and borders.
Numbers run in tight tabular columns: hops, tokens, time, cost.
Every answer states what it spent, right-aligned, like a running time.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Symbols are stars and Leiden communities are named constellations. Each answer joins its stars into a constellation. Ships with your Black/Blue/Cyan and Blue/White/Pink themes plus more, switchable live.
options.viewport: The graph owns the screen, communities labelled by name, the lit path as bright lines; chat docked right.
options.risk: The most familiar pick here: a dark starry graph is a look many developer tools already wear. Dense repos could read as noise.

options.label: Course Map
options.thesis: Parsed code is the terrain and never changes; the answer is a numbered course ridden on top. It makes 'facts first, narrative second' literal. Ships with your Black/Blue/Cyan and Blue/White/Pink themes plus more, switchable live.
options.viewport: Graph as a quiet map, numbered circles for the answer's path, and a control table under the answer listing each step and how it was reached.
options.case: Fuses well: ordered steps and an honest 'no route' row beat the core log on clarity, but engineers don't know this world by heart.
options.risk: Numbering implies an order, and cited symbols don't always have one.

options.label: Live Tiles
options.thesis: Flat colour and huge lowercase, no chrome. Your black and cyan at full commitment, with code areas as words and symbols as tiles. Ships with your Black/Blue/Cyan and Blue/White/Pink themes plus more, switchable live.
options.viewport: Communities as a giant cropped word, symbols as tiles, the path as flooded tiles; chat on the right.
options.case: The most striking fit for 'modern', but tiles replace the graph picture, and the graph is what the product is for.
options.risk: Loses the node-and-edge view that shows relationships. It may need a graph toggle.

options.label: Acetate Manual
options.case: Engineers read graphs here, not manuals, and its board colours fight your palettes.
options.kept: Rank comes from one system only.

options.label: Data Field
options.case: Pure black and white conflicts with the colours you asked for.

options.label: Mixtape J-Card
options.case: Charming, but handwriting costs trust for a tool reporting facts.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.case: One item at a time removes the overview that makes a graph useful.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished dark developer tool: side navigation, graph, chat, done to the standard of the best products in this category.
canonCard.viewport: Left navigation, graph in the centre, chat on the right.
canonCard.risk: Looks like its neighbours, by design.
